problem.text: Conversion previously consumed the allocator's per-projection bitrates directly. This change adds an experimental command-line mechanism for increasing selected projection bitrates in selected top-level modules.

reasoning.text: Projection-role labels decouple the modifier syntax from checkpoint tensor names. The labels, recursive module lookup and post-allocation transformation are cooperating edits: the converter needs all three to resolve a strategy key to its requested increment.

impact.text: The modified values become quant_args['K'] before individual linears are converted. The original allocator surplus is retained, so these additions are not compensated by reducing subsequent allocations. The diff explicitly leaves overall bitrate-increase accounting and checkpoint tracking as TODOs.

source_notes.text: The initial commit's modules and conversion chapters were read. They describe recursive module traversal, the Linear conversion interface and size-based allocation rather than an error-driven bitrate search.

The earlier conversion entry's duplicate work-directory prefix is absent from the inspected parent: main passes relative qtensors and checkpoint filenames to save_tensor. The task leaves those calls unchanged. Its recorded exact-budget allocation boundary remains in allocation.py, also unchanged.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” concerns codebook multipliers and includes experiments with per-tensor bitrate recipes. Its connection to this task is an inference based on the shared convert_model.py strategy-to-K handoff and manual projection increments; it is not an explicit link to this commit or evidence of this option's quality gains.

Other matched discussions report different failures: #33 “Error converting model” covers file-opening failure and later GLM sampling trouble; #34 “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” #42 “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” and #43 “Error converting abliterated Qwen3 mlabonne/Qwen3-30B-A3B-abliterated” concern invalid calibration states or factorization. Their relationship here is inferred only from shared conversion/Linear traceback paths, not evidence that bitrate modifiers fix them.

Likewise, #8 “RuntimeError: shape '[5120, -1, 128]' is invalid for input of size 776524800,” #11 “AssertionError: bias is wrong datatype,” #16 “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” #38 “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” and PR #13 “Fix a tokenizer issue while converting models without a bos_token_id defined” concern padding, bias dtype, tokenizer truncation, sliced loading and missing BOS respectively. Shared conversion paths suggest contextual relevance, not a causal connection to this feature.

limitations: No model conversion, GPU execution, quality benchmark or resume/recovery test was performed. The scalar check models parsing and integer arithmetic only.
The inspected source establishes modifier behavior, not an accuracy-optimal recipe or the author's precise experimental motivation.
Repository call-site inspection does not establish compatibility for external positional callers of Linear; the new parameter is inserted before fkey.

claims.text: -strat/--strategy accepts a string, with parser default None and prepared default ''. prepare stores it with the job arguments. Its normal nonempty changed value is not overridable on resume unless --override_anyway is supplied. The helper uses args.get('strategy'), so absent or empty values preserve the existing strategy.

mod_strategy prepends an empty entry to the semicolon-separated string and indexes it with enumerate(model.modules)'s index. Thus the first supplied segment targets top-level module index 1, not an independently discovered transformer-layer number. Empty segments make no increments; indices beyond the supplied list return the original allocation.

Each segment is parsed as consecutive two-character pairs: a role character followed by a single digit converted with int. Repeated roles overwrite earlier increments; unknown roles have no matching effect. For each strategy key, the helper finds the submodule and computes min(original_bits + increment, 8). Eight is the bitrate ceiling, matching the existing transformer allocator's cap; this is not a percentage or storage-byte limit.

Attention labels Q/K/V/output projections q/k/v/o. Ordinary MLP labels up/down u/d; GatedMLP labels each constructed gate/up/down projection g/u/d, including slices. These are separate from qmap, which groups shared calibration inputs, and qbits_key, which chooses the base decoder or head budget.

Module.find_module follows the existing Model.find_module pattern: return the first exact key match while traversing the subtree, otherwise implicitly return None. Existing test callers of the model-level lookup immediately load their named result without a missing-key guard. The new converter likewise assumes a match, but supplies keys generated by allocation from the block's own projections. Lookup runs before loading/slicing, against the registered module tree.

Whole-tree Linear call inspection found no existing call passing the shifted optional arguments positionally. Heads in cohere, cohere2, decilm, gemma2, gemma3, glm4, llama, mixtral, phi3, qwen3 and qwen3_moe use keyword arguments and retain the empty modifier label. BlockSparseMLP's routing gate and expert gate/up/down constructors also remain unlabeled: g/u/d modifiers therefore do not increase those expert projections. The default empty label preserves constructor compatibility but limits feature coverage.

A standard-library scalar transcription verified that q1k2 increases initial q=k=3 to 4 and 5, repeated q1q2 leaves a +2 increment, and q1;d2 affects indices 1 and 2 while leaving indices 0 and 3 unchanged. It also observed IndexError for q and ValueError for q-1. This did not execute the repository converter.

This is an additive experiment layered over the existing size-budget heuristic, not a replacement allocator. It trades explicit local control for loss of the original global budget accounting. Leaving the option unset preserves the previous allocation path; changing --bits instead continues to use the allocator's projection patterns and surplus propagation.

findings.description: Malformed strategy segments reach unchecked pair indexing or integer conversion during conversion.
findings.trigger: Supply --strategy q, or a segment such as q-1, and reach its indexed top-level module.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject malformed modifier syntax with an actionable argument-validation error before processing modules.
findings.actual_behavior: s[1] raises IndexError for an odd trailing character; int(m) raises ValueError for a nondigit. main calls the helper before loading that module, with no local error handling.

verification.description: Reimplemented the inspected pair parser and observed IndexError for q and ValueError for q-1.
verification.limits: No repository conversion ran. The direct caller is the newly added main call; no parent-tree mod_strategy callers existed.

findings.description: The inherited allocator can exclude an exactly affordable candidate; the modifier feature does not repair that boundary.
findings.trigger: allocate_transformer has a candidate costing exactly budget and a lower-cost candidate preceding it.
findings.expected_behavior: The largest option within budget should include an exactly equal-cost candidate.
findings.actual_behavior: bisect_right(options, (budget,)) orders the shorter search tuple before equal-cost (cost, pattern) tuples; subtracting one selects an earlier candidate.

verification.description: Compared the allocator with both direct callers, TransformerBlock.allocate_q and ParallelDecoderBlock.allocate_q, and the task's subsequent modifier call.
verification.limits: Carried-over source observation previously recorded in the initial conversion entry; no fresh model allocation execution or quality measurement.

annotation.summary: Adds experimental per-module, per-projection bitrate increments after allocation, with an eight-bit cap. Existing budgets are not rebalanced, sparse experts remain unlabeled, and malformed modifier strings are unchecked.
